subject.title: Telegram: unquarantine skipped sticker e2e tests

question: Should Telegram maintainers require a separate static WEBP sticker dispatch e2e test, or accept the current cache-refresh and runtime coverage as sufficient?
rationale: Current main already removed the explicit skips and covers cache-refresh behavior, but the named static WEBP e2e case is absent and the issue carries protected maintainer/product-decision labels.

options.title: Restore static WEBP e2e coverage
options.body: Add one deterministic static sticker dispatch test that asserts `<media:sticker>` and sticker metadata, then verify the sticker file in Linux and Windows lanes.

options.title: Accept current coverage
options.body: Document that the active cache-refresh test plus runtime resolver coverage is sufficient, then close this issue as a maintainer coverage decision.

options.title: Move to broader media test planning
options.body: Track static sticker dispatch coverage under a broader Telegram media e2e hardening item if owners want to redesign the harness first.

recommendation.title: Restore static WEBP e2e coverage
recommendation.body: Add one deterministic static sticker dispatch test that asserts `<media:sticker>` and sticker metadata, then verify the sticker file in Linux and Windows lanes.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh authored the quarantine commit and this follow-up issue, so he has the clearest provenance for the original coverage intent.
